text:
ajohnson: Heads-up — Aurora Finance is asking for a formal commit on Private deployment + KMS by end of Q3. They want hard dates for rollout and canary windows. They’ve asked for an enterprise SOW and SLA language. :eyes:

maria_p: Thanks. Do we have a proposed minimal scope that we can commit to? We should separate must-have vs nice-to-have.

devon_eng: Minimal scope I’d push: private control plane, KMS integration (AES-GCM via customer KMS), model pinning support, and basic observability (per-route latency + errors). No advanced autoscale for initial commit.

ajohnson: Aurora says they need model pinning, KMS, and SOC2 audit artifacts. They want a canary in 2 regions for 4 weeks. If we can't meet that window, they'll escalate.

sara_cs: I spoke with their security lead — KMS is blocker. They need BYOK and HSM option on the table. Also they asked for retention policy controls (30/90/365).

maria_p: OK. Proposed project plan (high level):
```
- Week 0-2: Finalize SOW + legal (sales/legal)
- Week 2-6: KMS BYOK integration + keys management testing
- Week 4-8: Private control plane packaging + install docs
- Week 8-10: Canary (region A) + telemetry checks
- Week 10-14: Region B canary + SLA signoff
```
This targets end-of-Q3 for initial canary.

nadir_sales: Legal will need specific SLA numbers. Aurora expects 99.9% monthly for Dedicated/Private. Can we commit to that for a pilot?

devon_eng: 99.9% for pilot is risky until we validate scale. We can commit to 99.5 for initial pilot and provide a roadmap to 99.9 once Dedicated capacity verified. We should put an automatic fallback policy in the SOW: if SLA not met, we offer credits or a remediation plan.

ajohnson: Aurora wants explicit rollback/escape hatches in SOW. They’re OK with phased SLA if we tell them up front.

maria_p: Draft launch criteria for signoff:
- KMS BYOK end-to-end tested with Aurora keys
- Model pinning works with version rollback in <5 minutes
- Canary telemetry shows latency P95 within agreed threshold for 2 consecutive weeks
- E2E runbook and oncall roster provided

sara_cs: Oncall: we need L2 on-call for first 4 weeks of canary and a named escalation engineer. Who can cover?

devon_eng: I can cover escalation for weeks 8-12. Ops-bot: reminder to add oncall rota entry for devon_eng during that window.

ops-bot: @devon_eng — rota entry created: weeks 8-12 (primary escalation).

maria_p: Risks to call out to Aurora and legal: KMS HSM availability per region, SOC2 evidence lag (audit cycles), and dependency on their infra team for VPC peering/setup. Recommend we include a dependency matrix in SOW.

ajohnson: Can we get a short one-pager SOW draft by Friday? Aurora execs want it before next exec sync.

maria_p: I’ll draft SOW skeleton today and send to legal/sales for comments. Will include the phased SLA language, rollback, canary plan, and dependency matrix.

nadir_sales: I’ll align commercial terms — target start-of-canary date is 2026-09-15 (tentative). If engineering needs more runway, I’ll push their expectation.

devon_eng: If we assume Sept 15 start, the schedule I shared is tight but doable if legal and infra approvals are parallel. Need a firm commitment from Aurora on their infra readiness by Aug 20.

ajohnson: Noted. I'll ask Aurora to confirm infra readiness by Aug 20. Will loop legal and cs. :thumbsup:

maria_p: Action items: 
- maria_p: SOW skeleton (due Fri)
- ajohnson: Confirm Aurora infra readiness (due 2026-08-20)
- nadir_sales: Draft phased commercial terms (due Tue)
- devon_eng: Prepare canary runbook + oncall (due 2026-08-30)
- sara_cs: Prepare customer-facing rollout comms and retention options (due 2026-08-25)

ajohnson: Thanks team — keeping this thread for updates. If anyone gets pushback from Aurora execs, paste it here.

sara_cs: Will do. :white_check_mark:
